archetype.name: Pocket Passer (intermediate attack)
archetype.definition: A tall, rhythm passer who wins from the pocket by driving the ball into the 10-to-19-yard window and taking selective deep shots off a run-leaning, often under-center offense, with his legs as a bonus rather than a foundation.

report.headline: Same aggression, far cleaner ball: Lawrence's career year looks mostly real
report.take:
Lawrence has never played like this. His 0.292 EPA per dropback ranks 5th of 54 qualifiers, his 8.82 yards per attempt ranks 4th, and both are well beyond his career norms. Before this season he had never averaged more than 7.2 yards per attempt, and his best EPA year (0.132 in 2022) ranked 11th. The production comes on modest volume: 28.8 attempts a game for an offense that passes less than situation predicts (pass rate over expected -2.8, 21st) and leans on a defense that ranks 4th in EPA. He is not piling up yards. He is making a moderate number of throws count.

The cause is accuracy, not a change in approach. His aggressiveness (16.73%) is essentially last year's, and time to throw dropped only 0.12 seconds. What moved was ball placement. His bad-throw rate fell from 13.9% to 8.5% (2nd of 42), and his CPOE swung 7.6 points to +5.68. That accuracy shows up where it pays most. Throws of 10+ air yards account for 76.5 of his 79.6 dropback EPA, with the 10-to-19 band at 0.618 a play on a 9.6 CPOE. Under center he has been close to flawless (0.501 EPA, 12.9 CPOE, no picks), which fits an offense built to make defenses respect the run before he throws. Parker Washington (64 targets, 0.434 EPA per target) and Brenton Strange are carrying the target tree. Brian Thomas Jr. has drawn only 26 targets at 0.181, a sign the efficiency doesn't depend on any one receiver.

The surface hides two things that will cool. First, the touchdown rate: 8.1% ranks 2nd and is about double the league's 4%. Twelve of those scores came in the red zone on 48.9% completions, a split that tends to drift. Second, the deep ball: 30 attempts at 0.965 EPA with a 16.2 CPOE is a hot hand on a small sample, not a baseline. He is also merely average on third down (39.7% conversions, 0.441 success) and in close fourth quarters (-4.3 CPOE). The pressure-to-sack rate (27.1%, 18th of 42) matches the middling sack avoidance he has shown for years. The last five games also carry a 3.8-point CPOE dip against his season mark, with three negative-CPOE games mixed in. Some of the accuracy surge is cooling even as the results stay strong.

The last three weeks (0.398 EPA per dropback, 10.72 YPA, 3-0) look like a breakout. They came against defenses ranked 21st, 19th and 29th today, in games Jacksonville controlled. The honest read: the gain in accuracy and decision-making is real and should hold at a high level. The touchdown pace (40 over 17 games) and the deep-ball returns will come down. He projects as a very efficient, mid-volume passer, not a 4,300-yard volume engine.

strengths.title: Intermediate accuracy drives everything
strengths.body: The 10-to-19-yard band is where his season lives: 0.618 EPA a play with a 9.6 CPOE. Throws of 10+ air yards produce almost all of his passing value. The cause is cleaner placement at an unchanged level of aggression, and that is the most repeatable kind of improvement. It held across the first half of the season against varied defenses.

strengths.title: Bad throws cut sharply
strengths.body: His bad-throw rate dropped 5.4 points from last year to 8.5%, 2nd among 42 qualifiers. CPOE rose 7.6 points. In earlier seasons he sat mid-pack or worse in bad-throw rate, so this is a real change. It also lines up with fewer interceptions per game, though not a dramatic drop.

strengths.title: Lethal off under-center looks
strengths.body: On 66 under-center dropbacks he has posted 0.501 EPA, 73.8% completions and no interceptions. That is far better than his shotgun work (0.209). The offense's run threat and 7th-ranked protection (hit rate 0.14) create clean, defined reads. As long as the run game stays credible, this looks sustainable.

concerns.title: Touchdown rate is running hot
concerns.body: An 8.1% TD rate ranks 2nd, roughly twice the league average. His previous best season produced 29 scores. The red-zone line (12 TDs on 48.9% completions, -3.2 CPOE) is efficient in outcome but not in process. Expect the scoring to cool even if the efficiency doesn't.

concerns.title: Volume capped by team design
concerns.body: Jacksonville passes less than expected and plays with leads behind a top-four defense. That holds him to 28.8 attempts a game and passing yards that rank only 12th. This is a cost of the team winning, not a flaw. It does put a ceiling on raw totals.

concerns.title: Accuracy slipping under the results
concerns.body: Over the last five games his CPOE is 3.8 points below his season mark, with negative-CPOE games against PHI, HOU and BAL. Third-down conversions at 39.7% are ordinary. The big recent returns lean on explosive plays, the least stable part of his profile.

trend.note: After an uneven start (a -2.9 EPA game at Denver), he has strung together efficient outings, capped by a 16.2 EPA, 352-yard game at Tennessee. The last three weeks came against bottom-half defenses and on short, controlled volume, so the rise is real but flattered by the schedule.

nextGame.headline: Leaky QB defense, but it takes away his deep shots
nextGame.body:
The Giants give up a lot to quarterbacks: 2.22 passing TDs a game (29th) and 19 PPR points a game (26th). They also barely touch the passer, with a hit rate that ranks 29th, so his pocket should stay clean. The catch is how they are leaky. They are the stingiest defense in the league against deep throws (-0.383 EPA) and hold yardage down (225.2 a game, 6th). Opponents run on them more than anywhere but one other team. Expect Jacksonville, already a run-leaning offense, to lean further on the ground as six-point favorites. That points to efficient, touchdown-friendly passing on limited attempts rather than a yardage spike built on shots downfield.

On his side, center Robert Hainsey (knee, 91% of snaps) is questionable after leaving the Titans game. If he sits, interior protection and under-center snap exchanges get less reliable, which matters for an offense whose best passing comes from under center. Against a front this light on pressure, that risk is smaller than usual. For New York, safety Jason Pinnock (back, questionable, 55% of snaps) is the only listed player who bears on the passing game. His absence would thin a secondary that has otherwise shut down deep throws.
nextGame.watch: Whether he finds the intermediate middle early against a defense that takes away the deep ball, or whether Jacksonville simply runs it and holds his attempts in the 20s.

restOfSeason.body: The foundation is solid. His accuracy gains (8.5% bad throws, +5.68 CPOE) come with unchanged aggressiveness, and his intermediate game has carried the offense. He should stay a top-10 efficiency passer. Two parts of the line will regress: a touchdown rate at twice the league average, and deep-ball returns built on 30 attempts. Volume won't rescue the counting stats, because this team runs more than expected and plays from ahead. Expect roughly 230 to 275 passing yards and 1.6 to 2.1 touchdowns a game. His rushing has dropped well below last year's level and won't add much.
swingFactors: How far the TD rate regresses from 8.1%
Game script: how often the defense hands him leads that cut his attempts

confidence.note: Nine games; accuracy gains look real, but TD and deep rates rest on small samples.
